key_insight: Combines the strengths of modular, hand-designed evolution procedures and flexible agentic search by explicitly accumulating and using evidence across iterations to guide candidate generation and prevent drift, improving long-horizon evolutionary workflows.
problem_solved: Addresses the trade-off between rigid modular pipelines (stable but inflexible) and general-purpose agents (flexible but prone to drift) and the under‑utilization of accumulated evaluative evidence in iterative program/workflow/scientific evolution.
method: Iterative generate-evaluate-feedback loop that produces candidate solutions and scores them over multiple rounds.
Aggregate and cache evaluative evidence across iterations to inform future search and reduce redundant exploration or drift.
Hybrid control strategy that retains modular reliability while allowing agentic flexibility for adaptive decision-making during long-horizon evolution.
impact: Makes automated evolution of programs, workflows, and scientific solutions more reliable and efficient by leveraging historical evidence to guide search, reducing wasted computation and improving solution quality over long runs.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram of the iterative generate → evaluate → feedback loop with an evidence cache feeding back into the generator.
Side-by-side comparison chart: rigid modular workflow vs. flexible agentic approach vs. proposed hybrid (trade-offs: stability, flexibility, drift).
Timeline showing accumulation of evidence over iterations and its effect on candidate quality/stability.
Icon set: candidate pool, evaluator (scorecard), evidence database, and controller/agent to convey roles at a glance.
paper_authors: Jiayi Zhang, Yongfeng Gu, Jianhao Ruan, Maojia Song, Yiran Peng
